# util-nd - n-d iteration and copy machinery

## Purpose

Low-level engine every read path bottoms out in. `NdCopier` (nd_copy.rs) moves a rectangular n-d
region between two byte buffers with independent non-negative byte strides. `NdIterUnordered` /
`NdIterUnorderedDyn` order, drop and coalesce dims and drive a 1-d inner loop with one offset per
operand (used by NdCopier, the elementwise pipeline, where, reductions). `NdIter` (iter/nd.rs) is
the ordered C-order index walker with pluggable extensions (stride offsets, block border sizes,
logical global index). `arr_ext.rs` builds/maps fixed arrays without copies; `arr_sequence.rs`
adapts `[Array;N]`, `&[Array;N]`, `Vec<Array>`, `&[Array]` and tuples to multi-array ops.
All strides are `usize` (bytes, or elements for `(1,1)` layouts) and never negative.

## Contracts

### PtrNoalias / PtrMutNoalias (util/mod.rs:647-760)
- They wrap a real `&[u8]` / `&mut [u8]`, so LLVM gets `noalias` + `dereferenceable(len)`; every
  raw-pointer access derived from them must stay inside the wrapped slice (provenance).
- `new(ptr, span)` (mod.rs:674, 722): caller guarantees validity for `span` bytes and, for the
  mut one, exclusive access for `'a`; for the const one, no writer for `'a`.
- `bytes_offset(offset)` (mod.rs:698, 752): `get_unchecked(offset..)` - offset <= len, else UB.
- `from_slice` is safe; non-overlap of src/dst is then enforced by borrowck at the call site.

### strided_span_bytes (mod.rs:109-118)
- Returns `sum_d stride[d]*(len[d]-1) + itemsize`, or 0 if any len is 0; itemsize for 0-d.
  No overflow check. Size-1 dims contribute 0 whatever their stride.
- `default_strides*` / `strides_for_layout_order` (mod.rs:120-190) produce C / layout-order strides;
  plain multiplications, no overflow checks.

### NdCopier (nd_copy.rs:15-411)
- `new(dtype)` (29-40) picks by `(itemsize, alignment)`: (1,1) u8, (2,2) u16, (4,4) u32,
  (8,4) [u32;2], (8,8) u64, (16,8) [u64;2]; everything else (odd sizes 3, 12, 24, zero-size
  structs, align-16 types) -> `copy_untyped` (byte-wise).
- `unsafe copy(src, dst, shape, src_strides, dst_strides, dtype)` (54-78). Documented Safety
  (47-53): each wrapped slice covers `strided_span_bytes(shape, its strides, itemsize)` bytes from
  its start; src and dst regions do not overlap. Implicit preconditions (NOT stated in the doc):
  - `src_strides.len() == dst_strides.len() == shape.len()`: asserted only on the iterator path
    (nd_iter_unordered.rs:68-70); the 1-d fast path just indexes `[0]`.
  - the `dtype` passed to `copy` has the same (itemsize, alignment) as the one given to `new`
    (only `debug_assert`ed in scalar_fn, 89-90; copy_untyped reads itemsize from copy's arg).
  - dst may contain 0-stride (repeated) positions; result is last-writer-wins, not UB.
- Alignment is never trusted from the dtype: the ALIGNED kernels are chosen only when both base
  pointers and all post-coalesce strides are multiples of `align_of::<T>()` (92, 108-110, 130-131).
- Empty region (any len 0) returns before any pointer math (64-66). 0-d copies one element.
- Responsibility for spans lies with callers: storage/compact.rs:392-484, storage/buf.rs:219-240,
  storage/elementwise_pipeline.rs:502-584 (Staging), array.rs:1318-1430, ops/shape_ops/repeat.rs:150-205,
  flip.rs:121-150, tile.rs:171-290, ops/sub_dtype.rs:147-164, util/bench_util.rs.

### fill_contiguous (nd_copy.rs:413-443)
- `pub(crate) unsafe fn`, no Safety doc. Real preconditions: `src` valid for `itemsize` reads,
  `dst` valid for `n*itemsize` writes, non-overlapping, both non-null (slices are built via
  `PtrNoalias::new`/`PtrMutNoalias::new`). Typed arms read `*src` even when `n == 0`.
  Only caller: Staging::fill_from (elementwise_pipeline.rs:544).

### NdIterUnordered<N> / NdIterUnorderedDyn (nd_iter_unordered.rs:32-299, _dyn.rs:13-240)
- Input: `shape: &[usize]`, per-operand strides (same length as shape, asserted), per-operand
  `(size, alignment)` in that operand's stride unit. ndim <= NDIM_MAX (DimArray push panics).
- Provides: every element of the region visited exactly once, offsets of all operands paired for
  the same logical element (multiset equality with C-order walk; tests 406-450).
- Order: dims of length 1 dropped (80-82); dims sorted by stride descending, operand 0 most
  significant, a 0 stride abstains, `None` (no operand could compare) is transparent
  (103-122, dims_sort_by 306-325); excluded operands (`new_with`, 62-67) skip the sort but still
  constrain coalescing. Nesting order of dims is UNSPECIFIED, but along any single input dim the
  index is visited in increasing order (strides unsigned, NdIter is C-order).
- Coalescing (129-150): consecutive dims (in sorted order) merge iff for EVERY operand
  `stride[group_inner] == stride[d] * len[d]`; group stride = innermost member's stride, group len
  = product.
- Flags (153-162): `is_strides_aligned[i]` = every post-coalesce stride is a multiple of the
  operand's alignment - says nothing about the base pointer (callers must check it, NdCopier 92,
  where_op.rs:192-197, reduction.rs:698-701). `is_contiguous[i]` = inner stride == size.
- Special shapes: all-size-1 or 0-d -> shape [1], strides faked as `size`, flags all true (84-94);
  empty -> shape [0], strides `size`, flags true (172-186).
- `foreach_inner_1d(f)`: `f(offsets, inner_len, inner_strides)`; inner_len and inner_strides are
  identical on every call. ndim 1 calls once with zero offsets - INCLUDING the empty sentinel
  (len 0). 2-d uses a manual loop (270-284), >=3-d an `NdIter` over the outer dims (285-297).
- Dyn variant: same algorithm, no `new_with`, offsets/strides as slices.

### NdIter (iter/nd.rs:14-180) and extensions
- Ordered C-order walk over `[begin, end)` per dim, u64 coordinates; asserts begin <= end and
  `check_ndim` (51-59). 0-d yields exactly one item; any empty dim yields none.
- Extension protocol (194-200): changes delivered right-to-left (wrapped dims as `on_decrease`
  back to begin, then the incremented dim); the final step also reports the run-off-the-end wrap.
  Callers relying on ordering (e.g. reduction.rs:535-545 "folded front-to-back") rely on this.
- `NdIterExtStridesOffset*` (strides.rs:10-158): `offset += S::from_u64(diff) * stride`;
  `from_u64` is a truncating `as` cast (mod.rs:86-88). Offsets are relative to the walk start.
- `nd_iter_ext_logical_global_index` (strides.rs:160-173): C-order linear index over `shape`,
  initial offset from `begin`.
- Extension list capped at 3; merging a 4th is `unimplemented!()` (nd.rs:370-379).

### NdIterExtBlockOffsetSize (iter/block.rs:22-141)
- Requires the NdIter bounds to be `[begin/b, calc_block_end(begin, end, b))` per dim (calc_block_end
  is mod.rs:608-617) and every `block_shape[d] >= 1` (else div-by-zero panic at 59-65).
- Yields `(inner_offset, size)` per dim: low border block `(begin%b, min(b-begin%b, end-begin))`,
  high border `(0 or begin%b, end%b - that)`, interior `(0, b)`. When `end % b == 0` the high
  border index equals block_end and is never visited.
- Callers: compact.rs:446-455, array.rs:1040-1046, 1353-1358, 1383-1390, reduction.rs:453-459, 545-551.

### arr_ext.rs
- `array_try_from_fn_inline` (11-58): on Err/panic drops exactly the initialized prefix
  (InitGuard) when `T: Drop`. `array_try_map_inline` / `array2_try_map_inline` (60-164): each source
  element is moved out at most once; unconsumed tail dropped by DropGuard on Err/panic.

### arr_sequence.rs
- `ArraySequenceImpl` (65-79): `arr` must be `< narrays()` (Vec/array index panic; tuples panic
  via 733-737). `narrays() == 0` is representable for Vec, slices and `[_; 0]`.
- `ElementwisePipelineTuple::N_OPERANDS` (131) must EXACTLY equal the count `operands()` yields:
  `to_buf_impl` (elementwise_pipeline.rs:137-139) only `debug_assert`s extra operands, so an
  under-count leaves operands without a cursor in release builds.
- `read_bulk_as_iter` (146-156): same Safety as `ElementwisePipelineImpl::read_bulk`
  (elementwise_pipeline.rs:52-58) plus: drop the returned iterator before the next call (Vec/slice
  impls reuse an `UnsafeCell` scratch). Only caller: ops/map.rs:345-356 (consumes it in place).

## Unsafe inventory

- mod.rs:674-679, 722-727 `PtrNoalias::new`/`PtrMutNoalias::new` - from_raw_parts; caller.
- mod.rs:698-700, 752-754 `bytes_offset` - offset <= len; relies on callers' span math (non-local).
- nd_copy.rs:77 dispatch through fn pointer; nd_copy.rs:99-102 (1-element read/write unaligned),
  119, 141-151 (bytes_offset per run) - rely on the copy() span contract (caller, non-local) and on
  NdIterUnordered offsets staying inside the span (local reasoning: offsets <= span - itemsize).
- nd_copy.rs:223-224, 281 `assert_unchecked(CONTIG == (stride == size_of::<T>()))` - established
  locally: pick_inner_loop receives the same flags/strides foreach passes (130-139, 108-118). A
  mismatch is immediate UB in release; verify every route (1-d path, single-element sentinel).
- nd_copy.rs:228-252 aligned `copy_nonoverlapping::<T>` / `read()` - ALIGNED chosen only after the
  runtime base+stride check (local). 257-271 `[T; LEN]` read - needs len == LEN (debug_assert only;
  holds because inner_len is constant per iterator).
- nd_copy.rs:297-349 untyped loops; 341-348 doubling fill copies dst->dst with n <= filled (local).
- nd_copy.rs:414-443 `fill_contiguous` - entire contract on caller; no Safety doc.
- nd_iter_unordered*: no unsafe; soundness of all consumers depends on its offsets (non-local).
- iter/*: no unsafe.
- arr_ext.rs:24, 52, 57 (write/assume_init), 34-39 (drop initialized prefix), 70, 93, 128-130,
  158-159 (`ptr::read` of source items), 83, 145-146 (drop tail) - local reasoning, guards.
- arr_sequence.rs:245-247, 342-344, 460, 584, 700 `read_bulk` - caller (map.rs) establishes.
- arr_sequence.rs:450, 574 `&mut *UnsafeCell::get()` - relies on read_bulk_as_iter's "drop before
  next call" rule (caller map.rs:345-356; non-local). 454-456, 578-580 `Vec::set_len` over
  uninitialized `S::Item` (see Suspicions).
- Related, not in scope: elementwise_pipeline.rs:280, 413, 550, 576 build PtrMutNoalias/PtrNoalias
  from raw pointers with `strided_span_bytes` / `saturating_sub` spans.

## Edge-case surface

- Empty shapes: NdCopier no-op; NdIterUnordered calls the closure once with len 0 and offsets 0;
  NdIter yields nothing (but computes `product::<u64>()` of all dims first, nd.rs:61).
- 0-d / all-ones: NdIterUnordered single run of len 1 with faked strides; NdIter one item.
- NDIM_MAX=8: NdIter carry ladder covers dims 7..0 (nd.rs:86); Dim<0..=8> only. Callers that add a
  synthetic dim (repeat.rs:42, tile.rs:58) guard `ndim < NDIM_MAX`.
- Zero strides: src broadcast (inner_loop_broadcast, inner_loop_untyped_broadcast), dst 0-stride
  (repeated writes), 0-stride dims abstain from the sort, 0/0 dims coalesce freely.
- Size-1 dims with arbitrary (even huge or 0) strides are dropped before sort/coalesce/flags.
- itemsize: 1/2/4/8/16 typed; 3, 12, 24, 0 untyped. Itemsize is u16 (dtype.rs:124).
  Zero-size struct dtypes exist (dtype.rs test near 1844): all strides 0, everything coalesces.
- 32-bit (x86, armv7 wheels, release.yaml:87-95): `align_of::<u64>() == 4` on x86 while
  `ScalarKind::alignment` hard-codes 8 for I64/U64/F64/ComplexF64 (dtype.rs:967-984).
  `Idx::from_u64` truncates; callers cast u64 ranges to usize with `as`
  (e.g. elementwise_pipeline.rs:200, 326; compact.rs:389; array.rs:435-436).
- Block iteration: partial low/high edge blocks, single-block ranges, begin == end, end % b == 0.
- Overflow: coalescing `s[d] * shape[d]` (nd_iter_unordered.rs:137), `group_len *=`, NdIter
  `nitems` and `remaining()` products - unchecked (debug panics, release wraps).

## Intentional behaviors

- Visit order of NdIterUnordered is unspecified; tests compare as a multiset
  (nd_iter_unordered.rs:406-450, doc 7-31).
- Empty region still invokes the inner loop once with len 0 (test comment nd_iter_unordered.rs:583-585,
  harness 398); doc at 45-46 says "visits nothing" meaning no element.
- Zero stride abstains from ordering (test 833); excluded operand still constrains coalescing
  (test 861); ambiguous comparison is transparent in dims_sort_by (test 877).
- Unit dims never block coalescing, whatever stride they carry (nd_copy.rs tests 745-760).
- NdCopier picks aligned kernels at runtime; misaligned bases are tested (nd_copy.rs tests ~525-600).
- Broadcast src, including along every axis (nd_copy.rs tests 817-847); fill_contiguous for
  itemsizes 1..24 incl. odd (852-866); zero-extent no-op (664, 870).
- The struct field-by-field copier was removed in 763a701 (#72); nd_copy.rs:9-11 doc and test
  comments (451-455, 797) still mention it - stale docs, not missing code.
- NdIter 0-d yields one empty index (nd.rs test 582); extension notification order tested 820-890.
- Tuple ArraySequence out-of-range `arr` panics (arr_sequence.rs:733-737).
- REQUIRE_ALIGNED is false on x86/x86_64/aarch64 (mod.rs:641-645): unaligned typed access is
  allowed there by design.

## Hot spots

- Coalescing (nd_iter_unordered.rs:129-150, _dyn.rs:91-107): can any combination of 0 strides,
  equal strides, or an excluded operand make two dims merge when the bijection does not hold for
  some operand? Is the group stride always the innermost member's?
- Do the NdCopier 1-d fast paths (nd_copy.rs:94-121, 372-386) and the iterator path classify
  contiguity/broadcast identically, so every `assert_unchecked` (223-224, 281) holds, including
  src==0 && dst==0 strides and the single-element sentinel?
- Callers' spans: for each NdCopier call site listed above, is the slice passed at least
  `strided_span_bytes(shape, strides, itemsize)` from the run start? Especially sub-slices made with
  `get_unchecked(off..)` (compact.rs:411, 477-478; repeat.rs:186-195; flip.rs:144-145;
  tile.rs:219, 262, 285; sub_dtype.rs:149).
- Order-sensitive consumers of NdIterUnordered: kernels whose result depends on visit order
  (argmax/argmin "a tie keeps the earlier one", reduction.rs:1638; float accumulation) are only
  correct if each output cell's stream is a single input dim or C-ordered. Does reduce_tile_impl
  (reduction.rs:679-689, sort by items/state strides only) ever reorder multiple reduced dims?
- In-place aliasing callers: reduction.rs:1153-1166 iterates out/state buffers that "may alias";
  unordered visiting is only safe if each element is read and written at the same offset.
- len-0 inner call: callers that derive steps or pointers from `inner_len` must early-return on
  empty regions (elementwise_pipeline.rs:209, 335 do; check reduction.rs:1159-1176 finalize/empty
  runs and where_op.rs:234-245).
- 32-bit: `as usize` casts of u64 ranges that size a buffer while NdIter walks the u64 range
  (array.rs:435-460 FnStorage) - does the buffer cover the walk when the range exceeds usize?
- arr_sequence Vec/slice impls: is `narrays * M` slots always fully written before the slices are
  handed out; can a user closure (map.rs `F`) re-enter the same pipeline while the scratch borrow
  is live? Do all `N_OPERANDS` formulas (225, 322, 426, 550, 688) equal `operands().count()`?
- Recent churn: 763a701 (#72, NdCopier rewritten to a single fn pointer, struct path dropped),
  e101fb5 (#67, broadcast staging + fill_contiguous), dae6c5c (#46, NdIter carry ladder),
  bb1ee2c (#84, block.rs doc only), 4645124 (#76, arr_sequence status plumbing).

### Suspicions (unverified)

- jix/src/util/nd_copy.rs:90 - `debug_assert_eq!(align_of::<T>(), dtype.alignment())` fails on
  32-bit x86 for (8,8)->u64 and (16,8)->[u64;2] since align_of::<u64>() == 4 there but scalar
  dtypes declare 8 (dtype.rs:967-984); debug builds panic on any n-d copy of i64/u64/f64/c128;
  release is fine (runtime check uses align_of::<T>()).
- jix/src/util/iter/nd.rs:61 - emptiness is `shape.product::<u64>() == 0`; an empty range whose
  other dims multiply past u64::MAX overflows (debug panic) and a non-empty product that wraps to
  0 in release silently yields nothing; `any(|&d| d == 0)` is robust. Same for remaining() 146-147.
- jix/src/util/iter/block.rs:10-16 - doc says block_end = `end.div_ceil(b)`; for begin == end with
  begin % b != 0 that visits one block of size 0. All current callers use calc_block_end, so latent.
- jix/src/ops/map.rs:238-247 - map_multiple accepts an empty sequence (stack.rs:63-65 and
  concatenate.rs:71-73 reject it); it then indexes `inputs[0]` (storage/params.rs:845) /
  `arrays.shape(0)` (map.rs:369) - index-out-of-bounds panic instead of an error.
- jix/src/util/arr_sequence.rs:454-456 (and 578-580) - `Vec::set_len` over uninitialized
  `S::Item` then IndexMut assignment: violates set_len's documented precondition (library UB),
  benign only because items are Copy/non-Drop and every slot is written before being read.

## Review units

Paths below are under jix/src/util/ unless prefixed.

1. util-nd-copier (~600 lines) - nd_copy.rs:1-444; mod.rs:107-190, 636-793.
   Consult: nd_iter_unordered.rs, dtype.rs:40-125 and 940-990, storage/buf.rs:55-110 and 210-240,
   storage/compact.rs:375-484, storage/elementwise_pipeline.rs:502-584.
   Focus: every assert_unchecked route; 1-d fast path vs iterator path agreement; aligned
   selection (base + strides) incl. 32-bit; untyped broadcast doubling bounds; itemsize 0/3/12;
   fill_contiguous preconditions; dtype mismatch between new() and copy().
2. util-nd-iter-unordered (~570 lines) - nd_iter_unordered.rs:1-326, nd_iter_unordered_dyn.rs:1-241.
   Consult: iter/nd.rs, iter/strides.rs, nd_copy.rs, storage/elementwise_pipeline.rs:192-340,
   ops/where_op.rs:180-250, ops/reduction.rs:665-730 and 1140-1180.
   Focus: coalescing bijection with 0/equal strides and excluded operands; dims_sort_by insertion
   logic; flags on the 0-d / single-dim / empty sentinels; static vs dyn parity; 2-d manual loop vs
   NdIter path; which callers are order-sensitive or in-place aliasing.
3. util-nd-iter-ordered (~840 lines) - iter/mod.rs:1-5, iter/nd.rs:1-520, iter/block.rs:1-142,
   iter/strides.rs:1-174, mod.rs:608-617.
   Consult: storage/compact.rs:375-484, array.rs:1020-1060 and 1340-1430, ops/reduction.rs:430-560,
   ops/shape_ops/flip.rs:100-150, dimension.rs:500-560.
   Focus: advance/advance_dim carry and wrap notifications; nitems/remaining overflow; 0-d and
   empty; block border math for every begin/end/b relation; caller bounds vs calc_block_end;
   from_u64 truncation of offsets on 32-bit; 3-extension cap.
4. util-nd-arr-sequence (~995 lines) - arr_sequence.rs:1-737, arr_ext.rs:1-258.
   Consult: storage/elementwise_pipeline.rs:22-140 and 940-975, ops/map.rs:225-400,
   ops/shape_ops/stack.rs:55-130, ops/shape_ops/concatenate.rs:60-150.
   Focus: N_OPERANDS exactness per impl; UnsafeCell scratch aliasing and set_len; empty
   sequences; drop/panic safety of the array map helpers; index validity of `arr`.
